Date May 29, 1933.

Subject (in full) Alleged Communist Quarters.

Made by D.S.I. Henry. Forwarded by [签名].

Sir;
When the attached file was received at this station,
enquiries were immediately made at the address mentioned, when it
was discovered that all the furniture had been removed, which might
have taken place between the time enquiries were made by C.D.I.
Prince and the commencement of enquiries by detectives of this
station.
Enquiries were continued and occasional visits made to
the house which is now occupied by one Wong Ching Yang (汪景陽)
also a doctor who can give no information of the former tenant whom
he claims is unknown to him.

C B Henry
D.S.I.

Supt. B. Division.

W.K.

A.C. [签名]

Date...........JAN 3. 29

Shanghai Municipal Police

I.O. CHINESE SECTION. Station.

MARCH 13th. 1929.

REPORT ON Alleged Communist Quarter.

Made by C.D.I. Prince. Forwarded by J.Klivens A.C. Pol.

Reference to the attached, inquiries shew that
the occupant of the house No. 53 Bai Tuck Lee (培德里) Tatung
Road, was one Tsang (張), whose full name cannot at present
be ascertained. The house is at present locked up, though
furnished, and Tseng (張) is reported to have gone, in
company with his wife, to Nanking. A written notice is posted
on the front of the house to the effect that the house is to
let, and that application for tenancy be made to Tsiang Yih Yien
(蔣伊寅) proprietor of the Sung Hwa. (華華) General Goods
Store, No. 724 Elgin Road. Tsiang Yih Yien (蔣伊寅) is
apparently a friend of the man Tsang (張) but when inter-
viewed refused to give any information of import with reference
to Tsang, or even disclose his correct full name. Tsang is
reported to be a foreign style Chinese Doctor, but so far as
can be ascertained he did not advertise his profession in
any way, and the people in the neighbourhood of No. 53 Bai Tuck
Lee, Tatung Road, could not, or would not, offer any information
regarding him that would help us in any way. We are informed
that Tsang and his wife left the house without paying the
house rent, but it is understood that they will return again
in the near future.

A.C.P. Pol'.
